narrative.overview:
Every dog is a naïf market painting of the kind sold on the street in El Conde and at the Mercado Modelo. The build shows one framed canvas at a time on a pale painted sky, set above two flat green hills. The frame is a two-tone gouache band whose edge is slightly wobbly, as if cut by hand, with faint brush strokes. Flat leaf silhouettes tuck in behind its edges. The dog's name is painted on the lower band in a heavy brush script, and the dog's facts sit beneath it in a white strip divided into cells. Everything around the canvas (the top bar, the thumb row, the sheets) stays quiet. It uses paper-white, night-blue ink and pill shapes, so the painting carries the color and the interface stays out of the way.

Density is low and deliberate. The stated aim is one painting, looked at carefully, with only a few taken home. Color works by strict division of labor. The frame paints (leaf green, mango, ultramarine, turquoise) belong to the dogs and the painted world. A single hibiscus pink belongs to the act of pressing. Ink belongs to text and to the selected state. The fills are flat: no smooth gradients, no glass, no blur. Depth comes from soft, cool, ink-tinted drop shadows under paper objects and under the canvas, which reads like a painting leaning off a wall.

The world explicitly rejects the dating-app stack: rounded photo cards with a red X and a green heart. Skipping is "Ahora no" (outline, a clock icon, on the left); saving is "Guardar" (hibiscus, a heart icon, on the right), and a save opens a reflection sheet rather than committing at once.
keyCharacteristics: One framed canvas per view; the photo fills about two thirds of the phone viewport.
Two-tone painted frame bands chosen per dog from a four-paint set, with a hand-cut edge mask and stroke texture.
Hibiscus is the only action color, and only on pressable things.
Shrikhand for dog names, titles and big numbers; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything else.
Flat gouache fields: sky ground, two painted hills, leaf silhouettes with one fill and a midrib.
Paper-white controls with pill shapes and ink outlines; ink fill marks the selected state.
Tabular figures wherever a number is read: km, counts, facts, slot pips.

rules.name: The One Pink Rule
rules.body: Hibiscus marks only things that act when pressed or dragged: the primary button, the save stamp on the draggable card, and the caret in a field. It never colors a heading, an illustration, a frame, a badge or a status. The color study found that the button-color effect comes from isolation, not hue (docs/color-study.md §1, "Red buttons convert better" is a Myth; the von Restorff effect is Strong). The pink works because it is the only one on screen.

rules.name: The Paint Belongs To The Dog Rule
rules.body: Each dog carries one frame paint pair (`data-frame`). That pair repeats wherever the dog appears: the canvas, the mini frame, its radar dot and its filled slot pip. A paint never becomes a UI state color.

rules.name: The Light Ground Rule
rules.body: Photos sit only on light grounds: the sky page, a white mat inside the frame, and mid-tone frame paints. Nothing near black ever goes behind a photo. This is cheap insurance for dark-coated dogs (docs/color-study.md, implication 3).

rules.name: The Never Color Alone Rule
rules.body: Skip and save are told apart by label, icon (clock or heart), position (left or right), fill (outline or hibiscus) and gesture direction. They are never told apart by red against green, and never by color alone (docs/color-study.md §4; WCAG 1.4.1).

rules.name: The Painted Title Rule
rules.body: Shrikhand is always set at weight 400 and only at title sizes (1.3rem and up). It never sets body copy, button labels or field labels.

rules.name: The Counted Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number a person compares (km, counts, ages, slot tallies, ring labels) uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Flat Paint Rule
rules.body: Painted fields (sky, hills, leaves, frame bands) are flat single fills. They take no gradients, no shading, and no shadows of their own. Only objects (the canvas and paper surfaces) cast shadows.

dos: Do keep hibiscus ({colors.hibiscus}) for the single primary action in a view. Pair it with an outline or ghost alternative, so it stays the only pink on screen.
Do give every new dog surface the dog's own frame pair via `data-frame` (hoja, mango, anil or turquesa), and repeat that paint in its pip, mini frame and radar dot.
Do put dog photos on sky, paper or a frame paint, with a white mat and an inner fillet.
Do set dog names, page titles and big counts in Shrikhand 400. Set everything else in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, with tabular figures for numbers.
Do keep a visible, labeled button with an icon for every swipe gesture, with skip on the left and save on the right.
Do use the ease-out-expo curve (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for state changes at 140–260ms and for larger moves at 420–560ms, and drop every duration to 0ms under reduced motion.
Do show selection with an ink fill plus a check or label change, never with a color shift alone.
Do mark sample data visibly (the DEMO tag and sample notes in caption style).
donts: Don't use a red X or green heart, a red/green pair, or any color-only distinction between skip and save.
Don't put hibiscus on headings, frames, illustrations, badges, statuses or decoration.
Don't place a photo on near-black or dark ink grounds.
Don't use smooth gradients, glass, backdrop blur or shading on painted fields; fills are flat (the slider's fill is a hard stop, not a blend).
Don't use hard offset shadows; shadows are soft, ink-tinted and negative-spread.
Don't add frame paints beyond the four in the set, or use a frame paint as a UI state color.
Don't set Shrikhand below 1.3rem or above weight 400, or use it for buttons, labels or body copy.
Don't shrink touch targets below 42px or primary buttons below 46px.
